statement: Sharp Fourier inversion on the two exterior lines gives the critical symmetric formula. The independent Selberg projection method gives separate half-axis convergence for p>1.
compatible_assumptions: Finite critical Mellin strip norm, original endpoint value bounds, and local H¹ in log coordinates for the contour theorem. Literal (A) and the norm imply the local condition. The Selberg route imposes the stronger p>1 weight.
already_proved: Ordinary inclusive symmetric convergence at p=0 including the smooth p=3 absolute-divergence witness, separate convergence on each half-axis for p>1, and signed failure for a continuous cusp outside the local and literal source classes.
new_claim_suggested: Determine whether the symmetric theorem survives logarithmically weaker strip weights, how far the local condition can be weakened, and whether the two half-height sums converge at smaller p.
conjectural_or_unresolved: Determine whether the symmetric theorem survives logarithmically weaker strip weights, how far the local condition can be weakened, and whether the two half-height sums converge at smaller p.
potential_counterexamples: The compact p=3 cusp defeats the norm and value hypotheses alone, with divergent local archimedean integral.
significance: Separates critical signed symmetric convergence with local regularity from the p>3 universal absolute trace. Luecking's Bergman embedding is context for the ambient absolute threshold only.
difficulty: Uses endpoint Fourier inversion and a good-height contour, with additional work needed for weaker strip or local conditions.
next_precise_step: Check logarithmically weaker inversion bounds and possible cancellation without symmetric cutoff.
tests: Sharp versus Gaussian inversion, folded ξ′/ξ contour, restoration of exact heights, Selberg estimates, and compact smooth approximation.

statement: An explicit positive-order divisor estimate combines with the Abel prime substitution to bound the finite (1,1) step in Lemma 8.
compatible_assumptions: Positive integer derivative orders in the convolution and real shifts |δ|≤1/2 in the finite (1,1) application.
already_proved: An all-positive-order convolution constant and an explicit bound for the combined (1,1) finite remainder.
new_claim_suggested: Allocate constants in the remaining steps to obtain a certified onset for the derivative-tail estimate.
conjectural_or_unresolved: Allocate constants in the remaining steps to obtain a certified onset for the derivative-tail estimate.
potential_counterexamples: The two-positive-order floor centering argument relies on vanishing weights at both endpoints. A zero order needs its own boundary analysis.
significance: Quantifies two reusable arithmetic steps in a numerical derivative-tail argument.
difficulty: Elementary for the finite estimates. A full onset requires additional contour and tail analysis.
next_precise_step: Bound the derivative gamma factors and associated contour errors with verified constants.
tests: Right-continuous floor summation, unimodality, a beta integral and the independently bounded Abel error.
